statutes_and_articles: Civil Service Law81/2016 Art69(6); Executive Regulation PM1216/2017 Art176; Constitution Arts170 and195; SCC Law48/1979 Arts48-49
subject: Termination of public employee for 30 non-consecutive days absence without permission; need for written warning and opportunity to provide excuse
disposition_or_holding: Court recorded that the Art69(6) issue had already been decided by SCC judgment 99/43 (8 Mar 2025); it treated the dispute as ended regarding Art69(6) and rejected the remaining challenge to Art176. The judgment states that the 2025 decision invalidated Art69(6) insofar as it did not allow the employee to submit an excuse for absence days for which no excuse had previously been provided; it did not invalidate the whole paragraph.
source_status: Full official SCC judgment text opened; 4 Apr 2026 session
legal_effect_or_followup: The operative effect of 99/43 was published in Official Gazette issue10 (repeated), 10 Mar 2025; the day after publication is 11 Mar 2025. The 2026 case confirms binding finality and rejects a fresh challenge on the same issue.

statutes_and_articles: Penal Code58/1937 Arts171,302,303,306; SCC Law48/1979 Arts48-49; Constitution Art195
subject: Constitutional challenge to criminal defamation and insult provisions following online publication
disposition_or_holding: Court held the challenge to Art171 inadmissible because that article was not included in the constitutional plea before the referring court. It held the challenge to Arts302,303,306 inadmissible because the constitutional issue had already been conclusively decided in SCC case16/24 (1 Sep 2025). Final disposition: الدعوى غير مقبولة.
source_status: Full official SCC judgment text opened; 1 Aug 2026 session
legal_effect_or_followup: The judgment reproduces the applicable statutory wording and penalty ranges and confirms that case16/24 rejected the challenge to Arts302(1),(3),303(1),306 as amended by Laws93/1995 and147/2006; no fresh merits review was undertaken in 115/25.

subject: Public employee termination for 30 non-consecutive days of absence without permission; opportunity to present excuses for absence periods
disposition_or_holding: Operative holding is quoted in full by later official SCC judgment 2/44 (2026): Art69(6) unconstitutional only insofar as it failed to authorize an employee whose service ends for 30 non-consecutive days absence to submit an excuse for the periods for which no excuse had been given; challenge rejected beyond that scope.
source_status: Underlying 2025 judgment not directly retrieved; holding and publication data quoted in later full official SCC judgment
legal_effect_or_followup: Published Official Gazette issue10 (repeated), 10 Mar 2025; judgment fixed the day following publication as date for effects (11 Mar 2025). The exact operative scope must be preserved; do not label all of Art69(6) void.
